This module introduces no new regulation, standard, or framework, and no new source was fetched
for it. It takes a single already-locked fact — the eQMS's (electronic quality-management
system's) own POA&M (plan of action and milestones) entry — and translates it for two audiences
without changing what it says. The links below are the direct inputs this module draws on; read
any of them for the actual mechanics, citations, and reasoning this lesson references by name but
doesn't redevelop.

- **[POA&Ms and
  CAPAs](../../grc-frameworks-and-risk-management/poams-and-capas/index.qmd)**
  (`grc-frameworks-and-risk-management`) — where the exact POA&M entry this module translates was
  built, field by field, from NIST SP 800-37 Rev. 2's Task A-6, and placed next to a CAPA
  (corrective and preventive action) to show the same tracking discipline in two vocabularies.
  Read it for the verbatim NIST text and the full reasoning behind every field this module quotes
  unchanged.

- **[Coaching your QA and reporting
  upward](../../directing-the-quality-analyst/coaching-and-reporting-upward/index.qmd)**
  (`directing-the-quality-analyst`) — where the "watermelon report" problem and the discipline of
  separating system measures from personal performance measures were first built, and where a
  management-review packet was first rebuilt around trend and aging instead of raw counts. This
  module's audience-translation instinct is the same discipline, aimed sideways instead of upward.

- **[Building an inspection-ready service catalog and
  CMDB](../building-an-inspection-ready-service-catalog-and-cmdb/index.qmd)** — this course's own
  module 4, which first showed that a self-identified, actively-managed gap grades differently
  than one a reviewer finds cold. This module's exec-quality-council translation leans directly on
  that same point.
